## McKinsey & Company (June 2025 to present)

He served as junior engagement manager on two of these studies.

### Logistics systems redesign, global electronics distributor (August to November 2026)

- Owned the systems workstream of a 14-week logistics network and systems redesign, as junior engagement manager on a team of two. Visited warehouses in four countries and led sessions with the CIO to map how current systems are used.
- Mapped about 100 systems and about 460 ERP integrations across 13 sites.
- Built the capability assessment grid and systems inventory that the team and the client's IT organization used.
- Built a future-state capability matrix to guide the systems vendor RFPs and shaped the target architecture.
- Wrote the systems chapter of the strategy, including its business case.
- Won the case for a site-by-site rollout instead of modular waves.

### Agentic customer-servicing strategy, Fortune 100 insurer (March to August 2026)

- Built the three-year roadmap of 112 automation initiatives behind the company's goal to cut servicing costs 30-35% by 2030.
- Showed that a lower budget cap would keep 74 of the 112 initiatives and give up only 3.1% of the modeled benefit. That finding reframed the investment decision.
- Built the LLM pipeline behind the sizing: an authenticated Playwright scrape, Claude structured extraction into Pydantic schemas, and taxonomy classification of 7,274 internal procedures. Scored 182 customer intents across autonomous, supervised, and human-led automation modes, with the scoring layer kept in plain Python for cost and auditability.
- Built a Python knowledge graph of about 1,500 servicing processes from wiki pages and Excel sheets. It links the extracted procedures to intents, call volumes, and costs. Led technical sessions with the client's CTO.
- Designed a first-contact-resolution measurement approach that set a baseline of about 80%.
- Boundary: he built the analytical system. The client's own engineers built the production servicing agent.

### ERP data-access benchmark, global enterprise software company (March 2026)

- Only associate on a seven-person, partner-led team; delivered in three weeks.
- Benchmarked how four ERP platforms let customers extract their own data, using a 10-attribute scoring rubric across deployment models.
- Designed and analyzed a 104-respondent survey of US enterprises and ran expert interviews with former platform practitioners.
- Normalized four structurally different vendor pricing models into one comparable cost view.

### Data-center and planning strategy, leading semiconductor company (December 2025 to January 2026)

- Mapped how data-center racks are sold and supported through direct, ODM, and OEM channels, including where the margin sits in each.
- Drafted the company's data-center business unit plan.
- Redesigned the company's annual strategic-planning process, benchmarked against three large technology peers, and delivered it in an executive workshop.

### AI pricing impact measurement, S&P 500 data-infrastructure company (July 2025 to March 2026)

- Owned impact measurement for an AI deal-scoring model used by about 750 sellers, as junior engagement manager.
- Built the Python and Polars counterfactual baseline that Finance signed off on. It adjusts for list-price changes, recency-weighted discount drift, deal mix, outliers, seasonality, and in-quarter timing, and treats new-product introductions separately.
- The method credited the program with a 2.2% return on sales in its first full quarter. He supported restating a higher preliminary figure when new-product history could not support the same adjustment.
- Handed the measurement pipeline to the client's own data-science team.

### AI compute economics research, McKinsey "Frontiers of compute" (February to March 2026)

- Built two cost-per-token models. The industry-wide model puts 2025 cost at about $0.14 per million weighted tokens, covering inference and training. The bottom-up model covers a 20,000-GPU cluster serving a 70B-parameter model.
- Built a six-lever scenario calculator that scores hardware and software innovations on cost per token. One scenario put the saving from custom inference silicon at up to 71%.
- Found that depreciation accounts for about 82% of AI compute cost.
- The work fed the published McKinsey article "Frontiers of compute: The technologies to reduce AI inference costs": https://www.mckinsey.com/industries/semiconductors/our-insights/frontiers-of-compute-the-technologies-to-reduce-ai-inference-costs. He contributed research and models and is not a byline author.

### Agentic quoting tool, now on Periscope by McKinsey (June to August 2026)

- The tool existed before he joined. He reviewed its FastAPI, Polars, and React pricing engine and documented 59 issues in 21 findings, eight of them P0.
- Found and fixed two paths that auto-approved deals below their margin floor, and added a 72-test regression suite.
- Validated the requirements model against six real customer RFPs, and made the optimizer suggest software and product changes before a price increase.
- The tool is live on Periscope by McKinsey and used by a global PC maker: https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/growth-marketing-and-sales/solutions/periscope/solutions/b2b-pricing-solutions/deal-execution-optimization

## IBM Consulting (July 2019 to July 2023)

### Senior Data Scientist (July 2021 to July 2023)

- Led a team of 5 engineers and owned the product definition and roadmap for an ML platform that forecasts employee demand and plans staffing. It went live in 18 countries, helped win a multi-million-dollar contract with a major US airline, and cut hiring costs by 10%.
- Built the testing and evaluation platform other IBM teams used to ship conversational AI. It handled 5M+ conversations in its first six months on Kubernetes and OpenShift and was adopted IBM-wide as a reusable asset.
- Led 4 engineers fine-tuning the underlying language models. Customer satisfaction rose 60%, and the share of conversations resolved without a human rose 15%.
- Led 3 engineers building an LLM-based job-skills matching engine, which shipped as a core module of the forecasting platform. Changing how embeddings were held in memory made it 75% faster.

### Data Scientist (July 2019 to July 2021)

- Built unsafe-driving detection from IoT data and a medical-claims classifier for a government entity.
- Also worked on anomaly detection in logistics, real-time firearm detection, and invoice-processing automation.
- Co-invented a computer vision system that reads analog gauges in changing weather and lighting, which led to two granted US patents.
- The system beat the existing approach by 30% on accuracy. He compressed the model with NVIDIA TensorRT to run on a Boston Dynamics Spot robot.
- Received the IBM Spark Award of Excellence, one of two recipients in India.

## Samsung Research America (May to August 2024, MBA summer internship)

## Open source

- Agentic Coding Evals: a harness in the style of SWE-bench that tests whether coding agents still pass a task after it is reworded without changing its meaning. The rewording adds vague specs, misleading comments, or distractor files. 16 tasks with hidden functional tests. Reports clean and worst-case pass@1, attack success rate, and cross-model transfer. MIT license: https://github.com/apurvg14/agentic-coding-evals
- Math Reasoning Evals: a benchmark that tests whether LLMs still solve math word problems after answer-preserving rewording. Numeric grading, worst-case robust pass@1, attack success rate, and cross-model transfer: https://github.com/apurvg14/math-reasoning-evals
- Tripwire: a monitor for teams of AI agents that finds the one that has been compromised. Five agents reconcile a ledger; one secretly inflates line items and honest agents sometimes slip. Tripwire breaks ties with a third agent and strikes only the odd one out. It fires an agent only after two strikes in the same direction, then redoes that agent's past work. Planted bait lines with known answers expose rogues that target big items. Over 1,000 simulated games per setup with scripted agents, it caught the rogue 94% of the time. It fired 0.10 honest agents per game, against 1.92 for a strike-both baseline. It left the ledger $53 off, against $5,204 for the baseline. Includes a live animated demo, a mode where Claude models play the agents, and simulations of honeypots and Byzantine fault tolerance. MIT license: https://github.com/apurvg14/tripwire-rogue-agent-monitor
